readings.title: Job's Present Humiliation
readings.subtitle: Mocked by the Base and Low
readings.text: [Job 30:1] “But now they have laughed at me, men younger than I, whose fathers I would have disdained to put with the dogs of my flock. [2] “Indeed, the strength of their hands, in which maturity has perished, what does it profit me? [3] “Gaunt from want and hunger, fleeing to a dry land, yesterday waste and ruin; [4] “Who pluck mallow by the bushes, and broom tree roots for their food. [5] “They were driven from among men; they shouted at them as at a thief. [6] “To dwell in the clefts of the wadis, in caves of the earth and the rocks. [7] “They brayed among the bushes; they were gathered under the nettles. [8] “Sons of fools, even sons of no name, they were whipped out of the land. [9] “And now I am their song, and I am their byword. [10] “They have loathed me, they have kept far from me; and did not withhold spitting in my face. [11] “Because <dn>He</dn> has loosed my bowstring and afflicted me, they have cast off the bridle before me. [12] “At my right hand the brood arises; they push away my feet, and raise against me their ways of destruction. [13] “They break up my path, they promote my calamity; they have no helper. [14] “They come as a broad breach; under the ruin they roll themselves. [15] “Terrors are turned upon me; they pursue my esteem as the wind, and my safety has passed away like a cloud. [16] “And now my being is poured out upon me; the days of affliction have seized me. [17] “My bones are pierced in me at night, and my gnawing pains do not rest. [18] “By great power my garment is changed; it binds me about as the collar of my coat. [19] “<dn>He</dn> has cast me into the mire, and I have become like dust and ashes. [20] “I cry to <dn>You</dn> for help, but <dn>You</dn> do not answer me; I have stood up, and <dn>You</dn> stare at me. [21] “<dn>You</dn> have become cruel to me; with the strength of <dn>Your</dn> hand <dn>You</dn> oppose me. [22] “<dn>You</dn> lift me up to the wind and cause me to ride on it; and <dn>You</dn> dissolve my substance. [23] “For I know that <dn>You</dn> are bringing me to death, and to the house appointed for all living. [24] “But <dn>He</dn> does not stretch out <dn>His</dn> hand against a heap of ruins, if one cries out when <dn>He</dn> destroys it. [25] “Have I not wept for the one whose day is hard? Was not my being grieved for the poor? [26] “But when I looked for good, evil came; and when I waited for light, darkness came. [27] “My inward parts boiled and did not rest; days of affliction went before me. [28] “I walked mourning without the sun; I stood up in the assembly, I cried out for help. [29] “I have become a brother of jackals, and a companion of ostriches. [30] “My skin has become black upon me, and my bones have burned with heat. [31] “My lyre has turned to mourning, and my flute to the voice of weepers.

readings.title: Job's Final Protest of Innocence
readings.subtitle: The Covenant with His Eyes and Hands
readings.text: [Job 31:1] “I have made a covenant with my eyes; how then could I gaze at a virgin? [2] “For what is the portion of <dn>Eloah</dn> from above, and the inheritance of the <dn>Almighty</dn> from on high? [3] “Is it not calamity for the unrighteous, and disaster for the workers of wickedness? [4] “Does <dn>He</dn> not see my ways, and count all my steps? [5] “If I have walked with falsehood, or if my foot has hastened to deceit, [6] “Let <dn>Him</dn> weigh me in righteous scales, and let <dn>Eloah</dn> know my integrity. [7] “If my step has turned from the way, or my heart walked after my eyes, or if any spot sticks to my hands, [8] “Let me sow, and another eat; and let my offspring be rooted out. [9] “If my heart has been enticed by a woman, or if I have lurked at my neighbour’s door, [10] “Let my wife grind for another, and let others bow down over her. [11] “For that is a wicked scheme, and an iniquity to be judged. [12] “For it is a fire that consumes to Abaddon, and would uproot all my increase. [13] “If I have despised the cause of my male or female servant when they complained against me, [14] “What then shall I do when <dn>El</dn> rises up? And when <dn>He</dn> visits, what shall I answer <dn>Him</dn>? [15] “Did not <dn>He</dn> who made me in the womb make him? And did not the same <dn>One</dn> fashion us in the womb? [16] “If I have held back the poor from their desire, or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail, [17] “Or if I have eaten my morsel by myself, and the fatherless has not eaten of it – [18] “For from my youth I reared him as a father, and from my mother’s womb I guided the widow – [19] “If I have seen anyone perish for lack of clothing, or any poor man without covering; [20] “If his loins have not blessed me, or if he was not warmed with the fleece of my sheep; [21] “If I have raised my hand against the fatherless, when I saw I had help in the gate; [22] “Let my arm fall from my shoulder, and my arm be broken from the bone. [23] “For destruction from <dn>El</dn> is a terror to me, and because of <dn>His</dn> excellence I am unable. [24] “If I have made gold my trust, or said to fine gold, ‘My confidence’; [25] “If I rejoiced because my wealth was great, and because my hand had gained much; [26] “If I have observed the sun when it shines, or the moon moving in brightness; [27] “And my heart has been secretly enticed, and my mouth has kissed my hand; [28] “This also would be an iniquity to be judged, for I would have denied <dn>El</dn> who is above. [29] “If I rejoiced at the destruction of him who hated me, or lifted myself up when evil found him – [30] “But I have not allowed my mouth to sin by asking for a curse on his being – [31] “If the men of my tent have not said, ‘Who is there that has not been satisfied with his meat?’ [32] “The stranger did not lodge in the street, I opened my doors to the traveller. [33] “If I have covered my transgressions like Adam, by hiding my iniquity in my bosom, [34] “Because I feared the great assembly, and the contempt of families terrified me, so that I kept silent and did not go out of the door – [35] “Oh, that I had one to hear me! See, my signature. Let the <dn>Almighty</dn> answer me, and let my accuser write an indictment. [36] “Would I not bear it on my shoulder, and bind it on me like a crown? [37] “I would declare to <dn>Him</dn> the number of my steps; like a leader I would approach <dn>Him</dn>. [38] “If my land cries out against me, and its furrows weep together; [39] “If I have eaten its fruit without money, or caused its owners to lose their life; [40] “Let thistles grow instead of wheat, and weeds instead of barley.” The words of Iyob_ are ended.
